entities.label: Person
entities.summary:
Marcus Valerius Messalla Corvinus was a Roman general, author, and patron of literature and art in the late 1st century CE. Born of unknown parentage, Corvinus rose to prominence during the reign of Emperor Augustus (27 BCE - 14 CE) and played a key role in the Roman conquest of Dacia (101-102 CE). He was a prolific writer, leaving behind works on history, literature, and philosophy, including the treatise 'De Re Militari,' which remains an important source for understanding Roman military tactics.

Corvinus's legacy extends beyond his military campaigns, as he was a patron of the arts, supporting the work of prominent writers and poets, including the poet Martial (40-104 CE). His influence can be seen in the development of Roman literature, which would go on to shape Western literary traditions.

The impact of Corvinus's writings and patronage can be seen in the many works he inspired, including the 'Aeneid' by Virgil (70-19 BCE), which would become a cornerstone of Roman literature. His contributions to the development of Roman military tactics and literature have had a lasting impact on Western military strategy and literary studies.

Corvinus's life and works serve as a testament to the enduring power of Roman culture and its influence on Western civilization.
